chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: Jimmy Blanton and Oscar Pettiford
summary: Whaley never heard Blanton but was close to Oscar Pettiford, and recalls telling Duke Pettiford was a soloist.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now did you know in that band Blanton. Was that before you.
Blanton, Blanton was there just before I came in.
Talk about this young man who was so great and so brilliant.
They told me about it. I never heard him, but they used to tell me that Blanton was great. I say how could he be. Pettiford to me was a great.
Yeah, Pettiford and I were like brothers.
Oscar Pettiford and when he went to Europe.
Tell me about it, because he was a dear friend of mine.

I told Duke -- when Duke said he had Oscar Pettiford coming, I said Oscar Pettiford is a soloist. He said well, he's going to play bass in my band and I said okay and he came in and you know how it takes time for him to get in the groove and --
And he got that cello, he could play that cello.
He's a fantastic player, a dear friend of mine. Fantastic player.
